accepted_gaps.title: No explicit delegation boundary
accepted_gaps.rationale: Task metrics rarely define when an AI may act, must abstain, or requires human approval.

accepted_gaps.title: Technical metrics are separated from care outcomes
accepted_gaps.rationale: Safety, downstream work, timeliness, understanding, and continuity are not captured by discrimination alone.

accepted_gaps.title: Subgroup failure modes are hidden by aggregate performance
accepted_gaps.rationale: Representativeness, labels, and deployment context can create differential harms.

accepted_gaps.title: Human oversight is unspecified
accepted_gaps.rationale: Authority, workload, override behavior, and escalation pathways need measurable definitions.

accepted_gaps.title: Clinical performance is treated as static
accepted_gaps.rationale: Deployment requires drift detection, incident response, update governance, and withdrawal criteria.

triage.rejected_gap: AI cannot contribute meaningfully to clinical care
triage.reason: Contradicted by task-specific performance and workflow evidence.
